claims.text: AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi is a magnetic high-entropy alloy capable of exhibiting a hierarchically decomposed B2+A2 structure.
The as-cast AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi baseline has a mixed or weakly phase-separated structure without a pronounced A2/B2 hierarchy.
Controlled post-casting annealing will enhance hierarchical A2/B2 phase decomposition.
Controlled annealing will increase the volume fraction of A2 precipitates within the B2 matrix.
Controlled annealing will refine or reduce the size of nanoscale A2 precipitates within the B2 matrix.
A2 is a disordered BCC phase that can occur as precipitates distributed in an ordered B2 matrix in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
Magnetic vortex states form within individual A2 precipitates in hierarchically decomposed AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
The ordered B2 matrix surrounding the A2 precipitates is weakly ferromagnetic.
Annealing-induced phase separation causes magnetic vortex structures to form in the A2 precipitates.
The interplay between magnetic A2 precipitates and the weakly ferromagnetic B2 matrix creates additional domain-wall pinning sites.
Magnetic vortex reversal contributes to the origin of coercivity in hierarchically decomposed AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning from the refined hierarchical phase structure will elevate the coercive field.
The annealed alloy will have a higher coercive field than a matched unannealed or as-cast baseline.
The proposed effect requires an alloy composition that permits B2/A2 decomposition.
The annealing temperature, time, and cooling rate must be tuned to increase the A2 phase fraction and reduce A2 domain size.
The optimal annealing temperature, time, and cooling rate may differ among high-entropy alloy compositions.
The quantitative relationship between A2 precipitate size or distribution and coercivity has not yet been established.
